name: Lux Capital
identity_check: Confirmed as Lux Capital (luxcapital.com), the venture firm co-founded by Josh Wolfe and Peter Hébert (Robert Paull listed as co-founder and venture partner), based in New York City and Silicon Valley (Menlo Park per Cooley), investing in emerging science and technology companies ('We turn sci-fi into sci-fact'); $7B under management after Lux Ventures IX (Jan 2026). TechCrunch calls it a 25-year-old firm known for frontier science and defense. Not Lux Research (an earlier Lux-backed company), not Luxin Venture Capital or Luxshare Precision (which appear in Chinese robotics round files in this repo).

thesis_text.value: Backs scientists and founders at the frontier of science and technology, turning 'sci-fi into sci-fact' and favouring conviction over consensus. Invests from the first cheque through late rounds and co-founds or incubates companies (Lux Labs). Fund IX targets the intersection of science, technology and national security: AI, defense, aerospace, industrials, transportation, energy and biotech.

open_items: No application form or pitch URL found: the contact page lists only general comms/IR/info mailboxes (not recorded) and no guidance for founders; accepts_cold_inbound left 'unknown'. The f(Lux) fellowship (luxcapital.com/fellowship) is a $15K non-dilutive grant for undergraduates, not a pitch channel.

requires_us_entity: nothing stated. The portfolio includes Tel Aviv-based Kela, Nigeria-based Terra Industries, Japan's Sakana AI and Bulgaria's EnduroSat (Q1 2026 report), so a US entity does not look like a hard requirement, but the entity structure of those companies was not checked. invests_in_indian_founders: nothing stated, left out.

portfolio_count_reported not found: luxcapital.com/companies features 28 companies (a curated list); the Lux Labs post says Lux incubated 'more than 20 companies'; Fortune (2023) quoted 40-50 companies expected from Lux 8. None is a reported total.
Check size: only the rhetorical 'first $100K and the last $100M' (Fund IX post); no typical cheque published.
SEC EDGAR refused the declared User-Agent (403), so Form D legal fund names, exact sizes and final-close days were not checked. Close dates are announcement dates; 2021 funds dated to the month.

A debut Lux defence-tech fund (Wikipedia cites PitchBook, 'eyes $200M', 2025) could not be verified: the PitchBook article returned 403 and Axios (2021 fund) also returned 403. Not fetched: the 2015 fund ($350M per a NYT headline cited by Wikipedia) and funds I-V.
HQ: firm pages say 'New York City and Silicon Valley'; Cooley (2023) gives New York City and Menlo Park. No street address on luxcapital.com.

Rounds not recorded for lack of a fetched round page: Nexus Robotics ($8M seed, Mar 2026, Lux per an aggregator that returned 429); XDOF ($70M, June 2026, Lux among investors per Robotics Roundup only); Physical Intelligence March 2024 seed; AMCA, Varda, Impulse Space, Valthos, Cambridge Aerospace, EnduroSat, Onodrim, Covenant, Tenzai (named in the Q1 2026 letter); Terra Industries' later $18M tranche (Aug 2026).

Terra Industries' $22M is called an 'extension round' (TechCrunch, which never says seed); recorded as stage undisclosed. Kela's $200M round was 'currently completing' per Globes' unnamed source (Kela did not respond); final close not confirmed.
Websites not confirmed on fetched pages for Kela, Terra Industries, Physical Intelligence and Nominal; founded year missing for Traysar, ConductorAI and Nominal.

Partner focus_sectors classified from their luxcapital.com bios (Wolfe: defense and biotech; Reeves: software/AI to defense and manufacturing; Farshchi: AI, semiconductors, autonomy, aerospace; Isford: physical world and software; Hess: technology and national security; Krishnamurthy: AI apps, infra and the physical world). Venture partners (e.g. Zach Iscol, Brett McGurk, Thomas Reardon) not profiled. Bilal Zuberi, named as leading Applied Intuition's 2024 round in another repo file, is not on the current people page.
